# Temple Scroll Column 26 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 26 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**26:1** And you shall make gates for the inner court — on the east a gate, and on the south a gate, and on the north a gate, and on the west a gate.

**26:2** And the width of the gates shall be fourteen cubits, according to the width of the wall of the foundation.

**26:3** And each gate shall have two doors, and the doors shall turn on their pivots.

**26:4** And the height of the gates shall be twenty-eight cubits from the threshold to the lintel.

**26:5** And you shall overlay the gates with gold, and you shall make for the gates coverings of fine gold over cedar.

**26:6** And the thresholds of the gates — of single stones, great stones, their width according to the width of the wall.

**26:7** And on each side of the gate you shall set pillars, and the pillars shall be of cedar, overlaid with gold.

**26:8** And each gate shall have a porch, and the porch shall be fourteen cubits wide and [...] cubits deep.

**26:9** And above each gate you shall make a chamber, and the chamber shall be for the gatekeeper who guards the gate.

**26:10** And the rooms for the priests and for the Levites — in the colonnades on each side of the gates.

**26:11** And the rooms on the south of the eastern gate — for the priests who guard the charge of the altar and of the house.

**26:12** And the rooms on the north of the eastern gate — for the priests who guard the charge of the house and who arrange the showbread.

**26:13** And the rooms beside the southern gate — for the priests who oversee the sacrifices and who inspect the offerings for blemish.

**26:14** And the rooms beside the northern gate — for the Levites who minister in the inner court with the priests.

**26:15** And the gatekeepers — of the sons of Levi — shall guard each gate by day and by night, and they shall not depart from their watch.

**26:16** And no unclean person shall enter through the gates of the inner court; and whoever enters shall be clean in body and in garment, for the court is most holy before Me.

---

*EMET notes: Column 26 well preserved. Gate specifications with four cardinal entrances. The fourteen-cubit gate width and twenty-eight-cubit height reflect the scroll's proportional system. Priestly assignments to specific gates organize temple personnel. Lacuna in v.8 for the porch depth measurement.*
